The interior's tree-like columns and spectacular stained glass are unlike any other church.

row.name: Casa Batlló
row.why_it_is_special: Radically remodelled by Gaudí between 1904 and 1906, this residential building is known locally as the "House of Bones" for its skeletal façade. Its undulating exterior, colourful broken-tile mosaics (trencadís), and nature-inspired interiors earned it UNESCO World Heritage status in 2005. Now features immersive galleries exploring Gaudí's creative process.
